paragraphs.heading: A student I never forgot
paragraphs.edited: I'll never forget one particular student that I had years ago in one of my apologetics classes. He sat in the back for probably the entire class, arms folded, feet up on the desk, looking at me like this is the dumbest class ever. Why am I here? I have to be here. I can't switch out of this class, and I'm stuck. I remember that every time I gave my lecture, or my talk, or the discussion — whatever we were doing for that day — I would focus it right on him, to make sure that I was talking to him. And I would look for little hints, little changes in the eyebrow or changes in posture and other nonverbals, just to see what he was thinking.

paragraphs.heading: How do you move forward?
paragraphs.edited: So now you need to figure out: how do you move forward? How do you go to the next level? How do you do the next sort of things that we have coming? It might just be to keep going — keep on to the next thing, keep on doing the next thing, and it's no big deal. But it might be that you put the brakes on someplace. Do you go back to an old lesson and revisit something? Think it through, and don't be afraid to make some adjustments if that's what you need to do. Because remember, there are going to be ebbs and flows, and there are going to be ups and downs. But the goal is to provide our students with what they need to be prepared to move the gospel forward and to proclaim the kingdom. That's the goal.
